bio: American author and commentator whose genre-bending novels have captured multiple Nebula and Hugo honors.

name: Naomi Novik
bio: American fantasy novelist whose folklore-inspired novel Uprooted captured the Nebula and Mythopoeic awards.

name: Cixin Liu
bio: Foremost Chinese science fiction author, the first Asian writer to win the Hugo Award for Best Novel.

name: Jeff VanderMeer
bio: American New Weird author whose Southern Reach trilogy redefined modern ecological weird fiction.

name: John Scalzi
bio: American science fiction author, three-time Hugo Award winner and former president of the SFWA.

name: Kim Stanley Robinson
bio: Legendary American science fiction writer renowned for hard-SF ecological realism and the Mars trilogy.

name: Jo Walton
bio: Welsh-Canadian author and poet whose novel Among Others won both the Hugo and Nebula Awards.

name: Connie Willis
bio: SFWA Grand Master and recipient of eleven Hugo Awards and seven Nebula Awards, more than any other writer.

name: Paolo Bacigalupi
bio: American biopunk and climate fiction author whose debut The Windup Girl captured both the Hugo and Nebula.

name: China Miéville
bio: British New Weird author and academic, three-time winner of the Arthur C. Clarke Award and Hugo winner.

name: Lois McMaster Bujold
bio: SFWA Grand Master and four-time Hugo Award for Best Novel winner for the Vorkosigan and Chalion sagas.

name: Neil Gaiman
bio: Acclaimed English author of modern mythologies across novels, graphic fiction, and screen adaptations.

name: Octavia E. Butler
bio: Groundbreaking American author and MacArthur Fellow whose speculative works pioneered Afrofuturism.

name: Neal Stephenson
bio: Visionary American author whose sprawling epics explore cryptography, linguistics, philosophy, and tech.

name: Vernor Vinge
bio: American mathematician, computer scientist, and five-time Hugo winner who popularized the technological singularity.

name: Dan Simmons
bio: American author spanning science fiction, horror, and historical epics, creator of the Hyperion Cantos.

name: Orson Scott Card
bio: American author, the only writer in history to win both the Hugo and Nebula Awards in consecutive years.

name: William Gibson
bio: Pioneer of cyberpunk fiction who coined the term "cyberspace" in Neuromancer and won the Triple Crown.

name: David Brin
bio: American astrophysicist and author whose Uplift universe novels captured both the Hugo and Nebula.

name: Arthur C. Clarke
bio: Legendary British science fiction giant, inventor of the geostationary communications satellite concept.

name: Vonda N. McIntyre
bio: Trailblazing American feminist science fiction author, three-time Nebula and Hugo Award winner.

name: Frederik Pohl
bio: SFWA Grand Master and four-time Hugo winner whose career spanned seventy-five years of speculative fiction.

name: Joe Haldeman
bio: Vietnam War veteran and SFWA Grand Master whose anti-war classic The Forever War swept all major honors.

name: Ursula K. Le Guin
bio: Towering master of American literature whose Hainish and Earthsea cycles redefined science fiction and fantasy.

name: Isaac Asimov
bio: Prolific biochemist and Grand Master of science fiction, architect of the Foundation and Robot universes.

name: Larry Niven
bio: American hard science fiction pioneer and creator of the Known Space universe and Ringworld megastructure.

name: Daniel Keyes
bio: American author and psychologist whose epistolary tragedy Flowers for Algernon won the Nebula and Hugo.

name: Frank Herbert
bio: Visionary American author whose magnum opus Dune became the bestselling science fiction novel in history.

name: Philip K. Dick
bio: Iconic visionary whose metaphysical and paranoid fiction probed the boundaries of human consciousness.

name: Robert A. Heinlein
bio: One of the "Big Three" of science fiction, inaugural SFWA Grand Master and four-time Hugo Best Novel winner.

name: Walter M. Miller Jr.
bio: American WWII combat veteran whose single published novel A Canticle for Leibowitz won the 1961 Hugo.

name: Alfred Bester
bio: American author and television writer who won the inaugural Hugo Award for Best Novel in 1953.

name: Lisa McInerney
bio: Irish novelist and essayist, winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction and the Desmond Elliott Prize.

name: Ali Smith
bio: Celebrated Scottish novelist, four-time Booker Prize shortlist finalist, Goldsmiths Prize and Costa winner.

name: A. M. Homes
bio: American novelist and short story writer, Guggenheim Fellow and winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction.

name: Madeline Miller
bio: American author and classics scholar whose retellings of Greek myths have sold millions of copies worldwide.

name: Téa Obreht
bio: Serbian-American novelist who became the youngest winner in Women’s Prize history at age 25.

name: Rose Tremain
bio: Acclaimed British novelist, winner of the Whitbread Award, James Tait Black Memorial Prize, and Women’s Prize.

name: Zadie Smith
bio: Acclaimed British novelist and essayist, Royal Society of Literature Fellow and author of White Teeth and On Beauty.

name: Lionel Shriver
bio: American novelist and journalist whose gripping psychological novel We Need to Talk About Kevin won the Women’s Prize.

name: Andrea Levy
bio: British author of Jamaican descent whose seminal novel Small Island chronicled the post-war Windrush generation.

name: Valerie Martin
bio: American novelist and biographer, winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction and Kafka Prize.

name: Kate Grenville
bio: Distinguished Australian author, winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction and the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize.

name: Linda Grant
bio: British novelist and journalist, winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction and David Cohen Prize.

name: Suzanne Berne
bio: American novelist and Boston College creative writing professor, winner of the 1999 Women’s Prize for Fiction.

name: Helen Dunmore
bio: British novelist and poet, inaugural winner of the Women’s Prize for Fiction in 1996 for A Spell of Winter.

name: David Grossman
bio: Acclaimed Israeli author and essayist whose kaleidoscopic novel A Horse Walks Into a Bar won the 2017 International Booker Prize.

name: Ismail Kadare
bio: Monumental Albanian novelist and poet, winner of the inaugural Man Booker International Prize in 2005 for a lifetime oeuvre exploring totalitarianism and Balkan myth.

name: Chinua Achebe
bio: Revered Nigerian novelist, poet, and critic celebrated as the father of modern African literature; winner of the 2007 Man Booker International Prize.

name: Alice Munro
bio: Canadian short-story virtuoso, awarded the 2009 Man Booker International Prize for her lifetime body of work and the 2013 Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Lydia Davis
bio: Renowned American short-story master and translator of Proust and Flaubert, awarded the 2013 Man Booker International Prize for her visionary brevity.

name: Annie Ernaux
bio: French autobiographical author awarded the 2022 Nobel Prize in Literature and shortlisted for the 2019 International Booker Prize for The Years.

name: Samanta Schweblin
bio: Argentine writer celebrated for her unsettling, surrealist fiction, shortlisted for the International Booker Prize for Fever Dream (2017) and Mouthful of Birds (2019).

name: Mariana Enríquez
bio: Argentine journalist and horror novelist, shortlisted for the 2021 International Booker Prize for The Dangers of Smoking in Bed.

name: Benjamín Labatut
bio: Dutch-born Chilean novelist whose hybrid non-fiction/speculative work When We Cease to Understand the World was shortlisted for the 2021 International Booker Prize.

name: Yoko Ogawa
bio: Celebrated Japanese author of over fifty works, shortlisted for the 2020 International Booker Prize for The Memory Police.

name: Fernanda Melchor
bio: Mexican journalist and author acclaimed for her searing, rhythmic prose in Hurricane Season, shortlisted for the 2020 International Booker Prize.

name: Bora Chung
bio: South Korean speculative fiction writer and Slavic literature translator, shortlisted for the 2022 International Booker Prize for Cursed Bunny.

name: Claudia Piñeiro
bio: Prolific Argentine novelist and playwright, shortlisted for the 2022 International Booker Prize for Elena Knows.

name: Eva Baltasar
bio: Catalan poet and novelist whose fierce and sensual novel Boulder was shortlisted for the 2023 International Booker Prize.

name: Cheon Myeong-kwan
bio: South Korean novelist and screenwriter whose sweeping, picaresque epic Whale was shortlisted for the 2023 International Booker Prize.

name: Selva Almada
bio: Leading voice in modern Latin American literature, shortlisted for the 2024 International Booker Prize for Not a River.

name: Itamar Vieira Junior
bio: Brazilian author and geographer whose generational epic Crooked Plow was shortlisted for the 2024 International Booker Prize.

name: Olga Ravn
bio: Acclaimed Danish poet and novelist whose workplace science-fiction masterpiece The Employees was shortlisted for the 2021 International Booker Prize.

name: Elena Ferrante
bio: Pseudonymous Italian author of the internationally bestselling Neapolitan Quartet, culminating in The Story of the Lost Child (2016 International Booker shortlist).
